video_title: Did Chandler Parsons ROB the Grizzlies of MILLIONS of dollars 👀

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons details his first knee injury, foot caught in David West's shorts, leading to microfracture surgery
quotes.quote: So the first knee injury I ever had, we were playing in Indiana. I remember David West had these baggy ass shorts, and I went up for a layup and my foot got caught in his shorts and I hit the ground really, really hard on the inside of my knee. I was playing so good that night, like 30-something points that night, and I was cooking. I fell and I used to wear these long tights, you know, like the long leggings on it, and I remember I ripped the legging and my knee was killing me. We had played OKC on a back-to-back the next night. I used to put the Normatec on, whatever. We fly to OKC and the same thing again. I'm just hoping, I'm just in the zone, I'm not even adrenaline's running. I feel nothing. I just remember after that back-to-back, I wake up the next day and I can't move, I can't walk. I went and got an MRI and from that fall, I had like a dime-sized piece of cartilage missing from the inside of my knee. And that's when they were trying to give me all my options and they said, 'You're going to have to have surgery, but if you can just rest for two, three weeks.' This is right before the playoffs start. 'Rest for two or three weeks, strengthen your quads, your glutes, your hamstrings. This is not going to get worse.' So, dime-sized piece of cartilage, not going to get worse. Three weeks later, we're on the Mavs, we get Houston first round. I had just left Houston. I'm like, there's no way I'm not playing in this series. So I do the proper rehab, I get it. Game 1, I remember like the second play of the game, bro, I go up, I dunk, I land and I just feel something in my knee just pop. And I knew it was so bad. I go, I get an MRI that dime-sized piece of cartilage that the doctor told me was not going to get worse, went to a quarter-sized piece of cartilage, which now required microfracture surgery.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons and Tony Allen discuss the brutal recovery from microfracture knee surgery

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: That's why he had that, bro. It's never the same. It's my knee and by the way, now I need like full knee replacement. My knees now are so smoked, but it's all because of that where it's just cartilage missing and just year by year, step by step, it just kept deteriorating and just getting worse and worse and worse, but it was all from that initial kind of fall in Indiana and that rehab.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: I had mine like probably like years before you had yours. So I don't know what's is it is it different like when you had it, you know what I mean?

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: So oh, what was your rehab like?

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: They had to go in and poke holes. Exactly, they drill holes in it. Drain and lateral release too, so they had to.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Oh, yours on the lateral side? So mine was on the medial side, which I don't know which one's worse, but I'm so bow-legged, like all the pressure is on the inside of my knee.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: And so I literally, I remember I couldn't walk for three months. I had to sleep in that stupid ass thing that keeps your leg moving all night and like you basically have to relearn how to move and play as an athlete.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons clarifies Memphis front office knew about his prior knee injuries

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: But to hear what I'm hearing now, it's like I get a better perspective.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: That is where the whole misunderstanding thing of my time in Memphis and my contract and everything. Chris Wallace, John Hollinger, the front office in Memphis knew damn well that I had had microfracture and knew that I had just tore my meniscus. I missed the playoffs. You guys know, that is public knowledge. There was no secrets.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Yeah, no, it was. But at the time, it's like it's Chandler Parsons, though. 40% from the three.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: 100%. Also, you're thinking I'm still going to recover because even after the microfracture, I still came back. I averaged like 15. I played, I was good.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons explains his free agency decision between Orlando, Portland, and Memphis
quotes.quote: Then after this, that happens, and that's where this whole misconception of like, oh, he didn't know about the injuries or they didn't know about the injuries. They fully knew about the injuries. The only thing they didn't do in that free agency meeting was it was coming down to Orlando, Portland, and Memphis. They all offered me the same amount of years and same money. And Portland had just gone through Brandon Roy and Greg Oden and all these injured guys where they were like on the fence. Orlando was my hometown, they weren't very good. I think it might even been like a three-year deal with a four-year team option. And then there was Memphis, who on paper, I was the perfect fit. You guys had this culture here. You guys were missing that shooting wing that can fill the gaps between you guys and Mike and Marc.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons reveals Memphis didn't require a physical before signing his contract
quotes.quote: This makes sense. And then this is where it gets a little hairy is Memphis didn't make me take a physical before I signed that contract. So all the fans, the people, they were mad at me. I just signed a deal because Memphis did not make me take a physical. It was public knowledge I tore my meniscus. It was public knowledge I had the microfracture. They were just I didn't want to say desperate, but they wanted to make a splash. They wanted to bring in a guy that they thought could be the missing piece, which I thought so too. I thought I was going to be a perfect fit with you guys. And I was also coming in off a surgery. If you remember, the first two months, three months, I didn't play. I was still rehabbing my knee. And so they were fully aware of all that.
